BRIEF
Date: 23JAN26
Analyst: Dance Monkey #2
Distribution: unlimited
Attribution: Bear Independent

The possibility of a transatlantic trade war has emerged from President Trump's aggressive campaign to acquire Greenland. Speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Trump seemed to back off from military threats, but still stated that Greenland is "imperative for National and World Security" and warning Denmark that if they refuse, "you can say no, and we will remember." Putting aside Monroe 2.0 and any potential for rare earth mineral access, the current threatening of a NATO ally’s territorial integrity represents an unprecedented rupture in the post-WWII order. If Europe cannot rely on the US as a security partner, the entire NATO framework comes into question, and when that happens, the post-WWII order becomes destabilized.

Already, 10 percent tariffs were to be imposed on eight European nations, including Denmark, France, Germany, and the UK, to start February 1, and these would then escalate to 25 percent by June 1. They have since been called off—for now. While these are called tariffs, they would functionally be sanctions, and the threat already created related impacts. In response to that tariff threat, European lawmakers immediately suspended ratification of a trade agreement that had been struck with the US just last July. In the words of European Parliament member Bernd Lange, "By threatening the territorial integrity and sovereignty of an EU member state and by using tariffs as a coercive instrument, the US is undermining the stability and predictability of EU-US trade relations."

European leaders were also considering deployment of their so-called "trade bazooka"—the Anti-Coercion Instrument—which could block US access to the EU's 450-million customer market and "inflict billions of dollars of losses on US companies and the American economy." French President Emmanuel Macron has publicly suggested this nuclear option, though implementation would take at least six months and requires agreement from 15 EU nations. The economic impacts would be significant since EU-US trade in goods and services totaled $2 trillion in 2024, averaging 4.6 billion euros daily. Europe's biggest exports to America include pharmaceuticals, cars, aircraft, and chemicals, while the US exports professional services, oil and gas, and medical equipment to Europe. Additionally, Europe could threaten to sell US bonds. While that action is unlikely due to the steep mutual cost, the threat alone would be enough to upset the bond market.

Currently, though, Europe maintains a heavy dependence on the United States. European NATO states received 64 percent of their arms imports from the US between 2020-2024, up from 52 percent the previous five years. Europe also relies heavily on American technology services, cloud infrastructure, and cybersecurity. Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Europe has become increasingly dependent on US liquefied natural gas, with imports jumping from 21 billion cubic meters in 2021 to 81 billion cubic meters in 2025, a nearly fourfold increase.

At Davos, Trump made clear that America's economic and military strength provides leverage European nations cannot ignore, but continuing to push this line against the US’s own allies may destabilize not just post-WWII stability but also post-WWII economic order.

BONUS INTEL
Source: Intel@BearIndependent.com

***

Yesterday Verizon had that nationwide outage, kind of weird but shit happens I guess. 

Well then we drove through the airfield at Fort Drum on our way home. Mind you I've lived here going on 16 years. I've seen days when there's helicopter maneuvers going on all day, sometimes a week or 2 at a time. I've seen planes practicing touch and goes, soldiers running the PT courses, convoys, soldiers training in the fields, etc.. you get the picture. 

What I've NEVER seen is almost all of this going on at the same time like I did yesterday! No planes but choppers in the air, soldiers running across the main roads with guns, AND the one thing I have absolutely NEVER seen before was 4 anti aircraft guns set up and being manned in an area across the street from the airfield. On any given day I would think absolutely nothing of seeing one of these things taking place. But yesterday a major communication system was down across the country with ZERO explanation and driving through the airfield witnessing so much activity really put a nervous pit in my stomach. It was a very unnerving feeling.

***

We live in a small town in Eastern South Dakota. In a recent update magazine from our rural water system, three of the seven articles were what could only be described as warnings. The first was how to build your own water filter, the second was about cyber attacks threatening small rural water systems, and the third, titled "What If?", was all about having a plan for if your public water service was "unable to provide service for an extended period of time." It sure seemed like a magazine full of indicators to us. 

Thanks for everything you guys do. The Patreon membership is worth every penny and then some!

***

I said in a previous email that I would check in with railroad Intel.Without naming names, a friend of mine from the Duluth MN/Superior WI (Twin Ports) area passed on some info from his company. The word is 'furloughs', with 19 employees being furloughed in the area. This makes for a total of 300 since the cuts started 18 months ago.

This company is known for its traffic over the US/Canada border to and from Chicago. Before Covid, there would be 20 or more trains in either direction in this territory. My friend says it now hovers around 12 each day.

***

Listen, major gasoline contamination at dozens of northern colorado fueling stations. Something to think about. Very easy for anyone to contaminate fuel tanks by dumping water right down the opening(fill holes)where the trucks connect to the tanks. A coordinated operation could shut down a good part of the country or the area that one lives in. Contaminated fuel will stop you dead in your tracks and the repairs are very expensive ! I believe the fuel supply would be just as easy to screw up as the grid. Maybe even easier.

***

A few months ago on our way to work (i work on a wind farm)… for now. 

We have been seeing blue strobing lights surrounding a major  substation in our area, this same substation had drones spotted over it at 4:45 in the am, last summer and it was reported to our sheriff ( i personally saw it, i reported it), it took off when our headlights pointed in its direction… anyways back to the point, i took a drive past said substation to find multiple 5 to be precise of those parking lot cellular security camera stations completely surrounding said substation. seems they no something we don’t or took the report seriously. 

Damage of this substation would cause a loss of power to a vast area along the washington oregon border and have a trickle down affect for many solar farms, wind farms, and natural gas power production facilities.

***

After hearing the national brief on 1/16/26. I recalled we had a similar instance with a middle eastern complected guy interested in buying machinery and scrap. 

We have multiple companies on site and one of the other companies was selling a lathe and mill. After this guy showed up, he was interested in buying electric motors, tungsten carbide, and solid carbide. Offered cash in hand. He took the stuff he could carry and left, and said he'd send for the machinery later.....never came back. This was in NW Ohio ...… 

Confirmation to previous sent Intel.....I talked with the guy at the other company and he said there was 2 separate instances like this. I am machinist as well and know that solid carbide and tungsten carbide is very hard  as it is used to cut metal. Possible shrapnel material?

***

Both my uncle and my brother are full-time employees of the US Postal Service. One in Tennessee the other in Alabama. Yesterday (1/16/26), they were both given new letters designating them as "essential employees". Same letters they received when Covid kicked off. Both asked their postmasters why these were being issued again. Neither had an answer but both postmasters agreed it worried them. My brother's postmaster said "it scares the s*** out of me because there's only a few reasons we would receive these, none are good".

***

You have stated you want intel from abroad as well so here you go. Over the holidays I was in the Philippines visiting family. Yes, I am well aware of the risks you have noted about commercial flights, but that is where my family was and for them, I accept the risks.

I have visited there off and on for over a decade, and while most Filipinos strongly distrust China, I have noticed a few things in this last visit that were new:

1. They are now opening car dealerships for Chinese cars. I specifically noted several for BYD.

2. An increased Muslim presence. Previously, there were a few muslim shop keepers, but this year I noted maybe 20% of the female shopkeepers were wearing muslim headwear.

3. The Philippines also has popular holiday markets full of people and with plenty of Christian symbols such as nativity scenes. While there were zero vandalisms of these and I am aware of no attacks, I also noted that there was zero security.

4. I have picked up some of the language and since returning I have noted that even their media often repeats the left-leaning messaging about the issues in places like Minneapolis. I have also heard their media expressing that the pursuit of Greenland will start WWIII.

***

Passing this along as a heads-up for aggregation. Just one data point, but it’s been repeating enough that I don’t feel good ignoring it, especially alongside other OSINT I’ve been seeing, and the range owner doesn’t seem to think it’s an issue.

I’ve been an RSO and instructor at a gun range in Michigan for about two years. Before that I was a Marine forward observer during GWOT in the Gulf AO then a 911 Dispatcher. I’m not claiming special insight, just explaining why certain patterns stand out to me.

About one to three times a month, we get groups of 4–6 guys who behave almost identically every time. Usually it’s one older guy (50s–60s) who speaks English and handles all interaction and payment, and then 3–5 MAMs who don’t interact with staff at all. The younger guys speak Arabic exclusively among themselves.The vibe is very much “work,” not recreation. No joking, no casual range chatter, no hanging out. They show up, shoot, recover brass, and leave. The older guy manages logistics; the younger guys just shoot.

Some consistent details that stand out when you see them together:

-Rubber/nitrile gloves worn before arrival, kept on the entire time, and worn out when they leave

-Extremely thorough brass recovery, well beyond normal reloader behaviorExclusive use of the outdoor bays (which don’t currently have camera coverage)

-Gear is modern and well maintained: common western service pistols and high end AR/AK pattern rifles. Suppressors show up sometimes (not suspicious by itself, just part of the equipment picture) 

-Shooting skill is solid and practiced, but not competition or instructor level.

What really gets my attention is the consistency. There are multiple groups like this. Sometimes it’s the same older guy with different younger shooters; sometimes it’s a different older guy with a group that follows the same script. It feels standardized rather than preference-based.

For context, the range is about 90 minutes north of Dearborn and just outside a mid-tier city with a Level I trauma center. We also have plenty of Arab and Turkish customers who don’t behave like this at all, which is why this pattern stands out.

I could be mistaken, but based on past exposure the Arabic sounds Levantine to my ear. That’s low confidence and just a descriptive note, not a claim of origin or affiliation.

Everything they’re doing is legal and within range rules. No violations, no probing questions, nothing overt. Still, taken alongside OSINT about mid-tier cities with Level I trauma centers being attractive coordinated targets, this feels like something worth flagging rather than shrugging off.

***

I live in a flight training corridor in north central Arkansas. It’s not uncommon at all for c-130s or even dogfighting to happen over our rural area. Dogfights are fairly rare but not eyebrow raising, C-130s are as common as cattle. Recently (over the past week) there has been a marked uptick in non-standard aircraft, flying non-standard routes, with either their ADS-B off or every major flight tracker concealing it at the behest of the D.O.D. The two aircraft that stuck out to me are a multi-engine small cargo plane I could not identify on Friday the 16th and a flight of chinooks as of about 11:45 local time. Both were observed flying unusual headings at unusual altitudes. They did seem to be observing the 500’ AGL FAA minimums but were low enough that the chinooks rattled the windows of our home.

***

Owner of the local coin and silver shop said he wasn’t buying sterling silver or 90% coins (1964 and older American Coin) because the refineries weren’t taking it to smelt. And the last last big individual buyer of it in the US stopped also. My point, got old American coins for $76.00 per silver OZ (actual silver content not just weight of coins) instead of $95.00 spot price today. Supply and demand. Just in case anyone is looking for a way to save money on silver.***
